chapter: On the road, James Brown and the 1956 crash
title: What caused the blackout, and the rescue at the crash site
summary: A doctor told Cobb that choking cut oxygen to his brain; he describes the tourist doctor's help, his pinned legs and seeing his baby.

story.theme_name: Illness, injury and the deaths of colleagues
story.community_name: Illness, injury and death among jazz musicians

blocks.x: When you had this blackout, it was due to coughing?

No, I said I swallowed up my saliva, and it hit my windpipe, and I coughed to kick it out. That's what blacked me out. Now, I didn't know until later, and I asked the doctor. I said, "What caused this." I told him what happened. He said it cut the oxygen from my brain.
: Oh.
That's what made me black out.
: But you -- you'd had no previous -- had you had a blackout before?
No, first time. Just a freak thing.
: Well, Arnett --
And haven't had one since.
: -- what happened? Did they get you both to hospital after that accident?
Oh, the tourist doctor, I told you, he saw that an ambulance -- he said, the ambulance will be here. He's the one that saw that an ambulance would come, and he told me to hold my head back.
: And your wife was bad too.

I never did see her on the scene. I just heard her moaning and groaning, but I couldn't move, you know, but I saw my baby because the filling station attendant had her, and she was redder than a beet, crying, like she didn't know what happened, and I'm looking at her and can't do nothing, but she's all right, really.
: Well, your legs were pinned by the engine?
I was pinned, my legs broken. I couldn't move them.
: But what broke them, the engine?
Huh?
What had broke --
The impact.
Oh, the impact.
See, the engine didn't come back in.
It dropped in the back of us, under us.
Oh, well, that was lucky.
Did you have all that terrible pain, or were you so in shock that you -- did you have terrible pain?
